item.title: The foundation is as scary as any SCP
item.content:encoded: I loved the end line, where the Agent was given amnestics and returned to field work. It's touches like that in pages that make me most creeped out, in a who-watches-the-watchman way - as much as the SCPs are dangerous and the Foundation is protecting humanity, the Foundation isn't safe, and disregard for individual humans/lives goes way past treatment of D-classes.

item.title: Staff Post: Reversion
item.content:encoded:
Doctor Song, 'scip' is a perfectly acceptable replacement for 'SCP' in informal conversation.
In addition "been disappeared" is grammatically correct in the sentence. Mann, the author, explains in-depth above, but basically it means he was caused to disappear by something else.
Before making edits to an article, please make sure you consider the author's intent.

item.title: Re: scip?
item.content:encoded: SCP is sometimes written as "scip" or "skip" when being used in dialogue. There is not a general consensus as to whether "SCP" is pronounced "Ess See Pee" or "Skip". Some prefer one way, others the other way, and some use both depending on circumstances.

item.title: Re: Small typo
item.content:encoded:
Nope. To disappear and to be disappeared are very different things.

If her buddy had simply disappeared, there would be many different possible explanations. Maybe he'd run away. Maybe he'd had an accident and was dead in a ditch somewhere. Maybe he was kidnapped by aliens. Lots of possible things could happen to do that.

That he was disappeared carries somewhat different connotations. Being disappeared is what happens to political dissidents in dictatorships. It's what happens to witnesses to a politician's corruption. It's what the CIA allegedly does to inconvenient people.

See the difference?
